metadata.disclaimer: Based on publicly available crosswalks and expert analysis. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance/audit use.

clauses.title: Policies for information security
clauses.rationale: SP 800-53 provides comprehensive policy controls (-01 series) for every family, covering cloud service security policies end-to-end. PL-01 and PM-01 provide overarching planning and program policy, while PT-01 and SR-01 extend coverage to privacy and supply chain dimensions relevant in cloud contexts.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly mandate a separate cloud services security policy; the requirement to address cloud-specific risks and shared responsibility in policies has no direct SP 800-53 parallel.

clauses.title: Review of the policies for information security
clauses.rationale: CA-02 security assessments and CA-07 continuous monitoring provide mechanisms for reviewing policy adequacy. PM-06 measures of performance and PL-01 policy review requirements directly address the periodic review of information security policies in cloud environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly require policy reviews to be triggered by cloud service changes or incidents in the shared responsibility model.

clauses.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
clauses.rationale: PM-02 senior information security officer and PS-01/PS-02 personnel security policy and position risk designations directly address assignment of security roles. PS-09 position descriptions formalises security duties in job descriptions, applicable to defining cloud-specific security responsibilities.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require delineation of security roles between cloud service provider and cloud service customer as mandated by ISO 27017.

clauses.title: Contact with authorities
clauses.rationale: IR-06 incident reporting and PM-15 contacts with security groups and associations both address maintaining relationships with external authorities and security bodies relevant to cloud service operations.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not mandate jurisdiction-specific authority contacts for cloud service providers operating across multiple legal jurisdictions.

clauses.title: Contact with special interest groups
clauses.rationale: PM-15 contacts with security groups and associations and PM-16 threat awareness program directly address maintaining relationships with special interest groups, threat intelligence communities, and cloud security forums.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud-focused special interest group participation or cloud security community engagement.

clauses.title: Mobile device policy
clauses.rationale: AC-17 remote access, AC-19 access control for mobile devices, AC-20 use of external information systems, MP-05 media transport, and SC-08 transmission confidentiality collectively address mobile device access to cloud services and the security requirements for devices used to access cloud resources.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly address cloud-specific mobile device policies such as corporate-owned versus bring-your-own-device distinctions in a cloud service customer context.

clauses.title: Teleworking
clauses.rationale: AC-17 remote access, AC-20 external system usage, SC-08 transmission protection, and PL-04 rules of behaviour together address the security requirements for teleworking including secure access to cloud services from remote locations.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address the cloud service provider obligation to support secure teleworking configurations for cloud service customers.

clauses.title: Relationship between cloud service provider and cloud service customer
clauses.rationale: SA-09 external information system services and CA-03 system interconnection agreements partially address provider-customer relationships. SC-36 distributed processing and PM-01 program management provide governance context for managing shared responsibilities.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no direct equivalent to the ISO 27017 requirement to document the shared security responsibility model between cloud service provider and cloud service customer, including explicit assignment of controls to each party.

clauses.title: Inventory of assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 system component inventory and PM-05 system inventory directly address asset inventory requirements. CM-12 information location and CM-13 data action mapping strengthen asset tracking for cloud-hosted assets and data flows.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not require the cloud-specific distinction of customer-owned versus provider-managed assets in the inventory.

clauses.title: Ownership of assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 component inventory tracks asset custodianship and AC-05 separation of duties supports accountability assignment. PM-05 system inventory includes ownership designation for cloud assets.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly assign asset ownership roles between cloud service provider and cloud service customer for shared or virtualised assets.

clauses.title: Acceptable use of assets
clauses.rationale: PL-04 rules of behaviour and AC-20 use of external information systems directly address acceptable use policies. MP-07 media use restrictions extend acceptable use to storage media used with cloud services.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address acceptable use of cloud service resources such as compute quotas, API usage limits, or acceptable data types for cloud storage.

clauses.title: Return of assets
clauses.rationale: PS-04 personnel termination and PS-05 personnel transfer procedures address asset return upon separation. CM-08 inventory supports tracking assets that must be returned or deprovisioned when cloud services are terminated.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to return or confirm deletion of cloud service customer data and configurations upon service termination.

clauses.title: Removal of cloud service customer assets
clauses.rationale: MP-06 media sanitization and PS-04 personnel termination address asset removal procedures. CM-08 inventory supports tracking assets for removal and AC-02 account management covers deprovisioning cloud service customer accounts.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no direct control requiring cloud service providers to define and communicate the process for returning or securely disposing of cloud service customer assets, data, and configurations at contract termination.

clauses.title: Access control policy
clauses.rationale: The AC family provides comprehensive access control policy and implementation coverage. AC-01 establishes policy, AC-02 through AC-06 cover account management, enforcement, least privilege, and AC-17/AC-21/AC-24 extend to remote access, information sharing, and access control decisions relevant to cloud service access.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly require cloud-specific access control policies that address the shared responsibility model or multi-tenant isolation requirements.

clauses.title: Access to networks and network services
clauses.rationale: AC-17 remote access, SC-07 boundary protection, AC-03 access enforcement, AC-20 external system usage, and SC-10 network disconnect together comprehensively address access to networks and network services in cloud environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to document and communicate which network services are available to cloud service customers and under what conditions.

clauses.title: User registration and de-registration
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management provides the primary control for user registration and de-registration. IA-04 identifier management and IA-12 identity proofing address identity lifecycle, while PS-08 personnel sanctions supports de-registration upon policy violations.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud service customer self-service registration workflows or provider-managed identity federation scenarios.

clauses.title: User access provisioning
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management and AC-06 least privilege directly address access provisioning processes. AC-25 reference monitor concept supports formal access provisioning review and authorisation.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly require cloud-specific access provisioning procedures distinguishing between cloud service provider-administered and cloud service customer-administered accounts.

clauses.title: Management of privileged access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-06 least privilege and AC-02 account management directly address privileged access rights management. AC-25 reference monitor and IA-04 identifier management strengthen privileged identity lifecycle in cloud service environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address the cloud service provider's privileged access to cloud service customer data and systems, or customer controls over provider privileged access.

clauses.title: Management of secret authentication information of users
clauses.rationale: IA-05 authenticator management, IA-06 authenticator feedback, IA-07 cryptographic module authentication, and IA-11 re-authentication together provide comprehensive coverage of secret authentication information management including password policies and credential lifecycle in cloud services.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to support customer-managed authentication secrets or customer-controlled credential reset procedures.

clauses.title: Review of user access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management includes periodic access review requirements and CA-07 continuous monitoring supports ongoing access rights review. AC-06 least privilege provides the baseline for evaluating appropriateness of access rights.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specify review frequency tied to cloud service risk levels or require customers to be notified of changes to access rights by the cloud service provider.

clauses.title: Removal or adjustment of access rights
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management and IA-04 identifier management directly address removal and adjustment of access rights. PS-04 personnel termination and PS-05 personnel transfer procedures ensure timely access revocation upon role changes in cloud service contexts.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address automated or timely access revocation triggered by cloud service customer requests when the provider manages the identity layer.

clauses.title: Use of secret authentication information
clauses.rationale: IA-05 authenticator management and IA-06 authenticator feedback directly address proper use of secret authentication information. AC-14 permitted actions without identification covers scenarios where authentication information must be protected even for unauthenticated access paths.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud user obligations for protecting shared credentials or service account secrets in multi-tenant cloud environments.

clauses.title: Information access restriction
clauses.rationale: AC-03 access enforcement, AC-06 least privilege, AC-24 access control decisions, and AC-25 reference monitor comprehensively address information access restriction. IA-04 identifier management ensures access restriction is tied to authenticated identities in cloud service environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly require cloud service providers to prevent access to cloud service customer data by provider personnel without customer authorisation.

clauses.title: Secure log-on procedures
clauses.rationale: IA-02 identification and authentication, IA-05 authenticator management, IA-06 feedback during authentication, IA-07 cryptographic module authentication, and IA-11 re-authentication together provide comprehensive coverage of secure log-on procedures for cloud service access.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud-specific log-on security measures such as geo-blocking, anomalous login detection notifications to customers, or federated identity log-on security.

clauses.title: Password management system
clauses.rationale: IA-05 authenticator management provides the primary control for password management systems including complexity, history, and lifecycle requirements. IA-06 and IA-07 add feedback and cryptographic protection requirements directly applicable to cloud service password management.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to support customer-managed password policies or self-service password reset integrated with customer identity providers.

clauses.title: Segregation in virtual computing environments
clauses.rationale: SC-39 process isolation and SI-16 memory protection address virtual environment segregation at the OS level. AC-04 information flow enforcement and SC-07 boundary protection support network-level segregation between cloud tenants.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no controls specifically addressing hypervisor security, virtual machine escape prevention, or multi-tenant isolation guarantees unique to cloud infrastructure providers.

clauses.title: Virtual machine hardening
clauses.rationale: CM-06 configuration settings and CM-07 least functionality directly address virtual machine hardening. SI-02 flaw remediation, SC-05 denial of service protection, and SA-08 security engineering principles extend hardening coverage to patching and secure configuration of cloud virtual machine images.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to maintain and publish hardened base image standards or provide customers with guidance on virtual machine hardening for their cloud workloads.

clauses.title: Policy on the use of cryptographic controls
clauses.rationale: SC-12 cryptographic key establishment and management, SC-13 cryptographic protection, and SC-28 protection of information at rest together provide comprehensive coverage of cryptographic control policy requirements applicable to cloud data protection.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not explicitly require a cloud-specific cryptography policy addressing customer-managed encryption keys, bring-your-own-key scenarios, or cloud service provider encryption key management transparency.

clauses.title: Key management
clauses.rationale: SC-12 cryptographic key establishment and management is the primary control for key management. SC-13 cryptographic protection, SC-17 public key infrastructure certificates, and SC-28 protection at rest provide comprehensive cryptographic key lifecycle management applicable to cloud key management services.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud service customer control over encryption keys, hardware security module integration, or key escrow limitations in multi-tenant cloud environments.

clauses.title: Removal of assets
clauses.rationale: MP-06 media sanitization and PS-04 personnel termination procedures directly address asset removal. CM-08 system component inventory supports tracking and confirming removal of cloud service assets upon decommissioning.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud service provider obligations to confirm and certify removal of cloud service customer data and virtual assets at contract termination.

clauses.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
clauses.rationale: MP-06 media sanitization directly addresses secure disposal and re-use of equipment including storage media. SI-12 information handling and retention complements disposal requirements by ensuring data is retained only as long as required before secure disposal.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud service provider obligations to certify secure disposal of physical infrastructure hosting cloud service customer data in multi-tenant environments.

clauses.title: Documented operating procedures
clauses.rationale: CM-01 configuration management policy, CM-02 baseline configurations, CM-06 configuration settings, and SA-05 system documentation collectively address documented operating procedures. PM-01 information security program plan provides the overarching programme documentation framework for cloud operations.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to make operating procedures available to cloud service customers or document cloud-specific operational procedures for customer transparency.

clauses.title: Change management
clauses.rationale: CM-03 configuration change control, CM-04 security impact analysis, SA-10 developer configuration management, and CM-05 access restrictions for change together provide comprehensive change management coverage applicable to cloud service configuration changes.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to notify cloud service customers of planned changes that may affect their services or to provide customer-accessible change management records.

clauses.title: Capacity management
clauses.rationale: CP-02 contingency plan addresses capacity planning requirements. SC-05 denial of service protection and PE-11 emergency power support resilience aspects of capacity management. CP-07 alternate processing site provides capacity redundancy.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud elasticity capacity planning, auto-scaling governance, or customer visibility into cloud service provider capacity limits and thresholds.

clauses.title: Event logging
clauses.rationale: AU-02 event logging, AU-03 content of audit records, AU-08 time stamps, and AU-12 audit record generation provide comprehensive event logging requirements. These controls map directly to cloud service event logging obligations for both provider and customer environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to make event logs available to cloud service customers for their hosted services or to define log retention periods aligned with customer audit requirements.

clauses.title: Protection of log information
clauses.rationale: AU-09 protection of audit information directly addresses log protection from unauthorised access and tampering. AU-03 audit record content and AU-11 audit record retention extend protection across the log lifecycle in cloud service environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud service customer access to and control over log integrity protections when logs are managed by the cloud service provider.

clauses.title: Administrator and operator logs
clauses.rationale: AU-02 event logging, AU-03 audit record content, and AU-12 audit record generation address administrator activity logging. AC-06 least privilege supports the review of privileged administrator actions in cloud service environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to log and make available to customers the administrative actions performed by provider personnel on customer cloud environments.

clauses.title: Clock synchronisation
clauses.rationale: AU-08 time stamps directly addresses clock synchronisation requirements, mandating use of authoritative time sources for audit record timestamps. This control comprehensively covers the ISO 27017 requirement for consistent time synchronisation across cloud service systems.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 AU-08 does not specify requirements for cloud service providers to synchronise clocks across geographically distributed cloud regions or document time synchronisation sources to cloud service customers.

clauses.title: Administrator's operational security
clauses.rationale: AC-06 least privilege, AC-05 separation of duties, CM-05 access restrictions for change, PS-06 access agreements, and AU-09 protection of audit information address cloud administrator operational security requirements including privilege restrictions and accountability.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no direct control requiring cloud service providers to implement specific security measures for cloud platform administrators with access to cloud service customer data, such as just-in-time access or customer-approved administrative sessions.

clauses.title: Monitoring of cloud services
clauses.rationale: AU-06 audit review and analysis, SI-04 system monitoring, CA-07 continuous monitoring, AU-12 audit generation, and AU-02 event logging together provide comprehensive coverage of cloud service monitoring requirements for both operational and security monitoring.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to share monitoring data or metrics with cloud service customers, or to provide customer-accessible monitoring dashboards and alerting capabilities.

clauses.title: Network controls
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection, SC-20 secure name/address resolution, SC-21 secure name resolution for users, and SC-22 architecture and provisioning for name resolution services provide strong network control coverage applicable to cloud service network security requirements.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud virtual network controls such as security group configuration, virtual private cloud isolation, or software-defined networking security in multi-tenant cloud environments.

clauses.title: Security of network services
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection and SC-08 transmission confidentiality address network service security. SA-09 external information system services and AC-04 information flow enforcement extend coverage to cloud network services provided by third parties and inter-cloud data flows.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to document and contractually commit to the security characteristics of network services provided to cloud service customers.

clauses.title: Segregation in networks
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection and AC-04 information flow enforcement directly address network segregation requirements. SC-39 process isolation extends segregation concepts to virtual environments relevant to cloud multi-tenant network isolation.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically address cloud virtual network segregation mechanisms such as VLAN isolation, virtual private cloud boundaries, or software-defined perimeters in multi-tenant cloud deployments.

clauses.title: Alignment of security management for virtual and physical networks
clauses.rationale: SC-07 boundary protection and AC-04 information flow enforcement cover both virtual and physical network security management. SC-06 resource availability and SI-16 memory protection extend to virtual infrastructure. SC-46 cross-domain filter addresses policy alignment across security domains.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no direct control requiring alignment of security management policies across physical and virtual network components in cloud environments, or requiring cloud service providers to maintain consistent security controls across software-defined networking layers.

clauses.title: Information security policy for supplier relationships
clauses.rationale: SA-04 acquisition requirements, SA-09 external information system services, SR-01 supply chain risk management policy, SR-02 supply chain risk management plan, SR-03 supply chain controls, and SR-05 acquisition strategies provide comprehensive coverage of supplier relationship security policy requirements applicable to cloud service supply chains.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to extend their supplier security policies to cover sub-processors or fourth-party cloud service dependencies.

clauses.title: Reporting information security weaknesses
clauses.rationale: IR-06 incident reporting and IR-04 incident handling directly address reporting of security weaknesses and vulnerabilities. AU-06 audit review and analysis supports identification of weaknesses through log monitoring in cloud service environments.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 does not specifically require cloud service providers to establish a vulnerability disclosure programme or provide customers with a channel to report security weaknesses observed in cloud services.

clauses.title: Identification of applicable legislation and contractual requirements
clauses.rationale: PM-01 information security program and PL-04 rules of behaviour partially address compliance identification. CA-02 security assessments and SA-04 acquisition requirements include compliance review. PM-08 critical infrastructure plan provides regulatory awareness context.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 has no comprehensive control requiring systematic identification of all applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to cloud service operations across multiple jurisdictions, which is the primary intent of ISO 27017 clause 18.1.1.
